open_change.name: open_change
open_change.description:
Open a NEW change from `rationale` (the task in one sentence, as the dev put it), or resume an open one with `change_id` (listed in get_pending's `openChanges`). This session's plan writes tag to it from here; `mark_implemented {change}` folds exactly its entries. Open one before any task beyond a one-line fix: plan writes are refused while no change is open.
Rules: change-ledger, loop-plan

change_id.description: Resume an EXISTING open change by id instead.

rationale.description: Open a NEW change: the task in one sentence, as the dev put it.

update_source_map.name: update_source_map
update_source_map.description:
Write the code-side mapping: `entries` (implementation anchors keyed by responsibility id), `test_entries` (attached tests, same shape, `pattern` = test file and `symbol` = the test), `schemas` (schema declarations keyed by node id), `boundaries` (directory globs keyed by node id). An empty `locations`/`sources` array clears an entry. Also the tool to attach a test AFTER a fold.
Rules: source-map, anchor-completeness, test-attachment

sources.description: Boundary globs the node owns; empty clears.

locations.description: Declaration location: `pattern` = file, `symbol` = the type name; empty clears.

Source.description:
A source-file pointer attached to a node. Wide glob + optional comment;
distinct from [`SourceLocation`], which carries precise line numbers.

symbol.description: Enclosing definition name; the durable anchor.

locations.description: Source locations; empty clears the entry.

test_entries.description: Attached tests keyed by responsibility id; `pattern` = test file, `symbol` = test name; empty clears.

ingest_test_report.name: ingest_test_report
ingest_test_report.description:
Report a finished test run: point at the JUnit XML file the runner wrote and every attached test's result is recorded against its claim — ONE call per report file. Verdicts are fingerprint-keyed, so a later edit to implementation or test flips them to stale. Reports what settled, what did not (unmatched, ambiguous, unmentioned), and the remaining radius. Call after every run.
Rules: test-verdicts, test-attachment

path.description: The JUnit XML report file, absolute or project-relative.

locate.name: locate
locate.description:
Reverse lookup from code into the model. Given a project-relative `file` (and optional `symbol`), returns in ONE call: the claims anchored there (with tests, `untested`, stale/vagrant flags; a test file returns the claims it is attached to), the owning node chain, the boundary owner, BINDING directives (own + inherited), pending entries touching those elements, and `scopeHealth`. Reads the working view. The single-file form of orient.
Rules: orient-phases, directives-binding, test-attachment

file.description: Project-relative source file to look up.

symbol.description: Identifier to narrow to; returns only the claims anchored to that symbol when any are.

get_test_radius.name: get_test_radius
get_test_radius.description:
Which test files actually NEED running: those attached to claims whose verdict is missing or stale. Run exactly those with the JUnit reporter on, then ingest_test_report each result file. Empty means every attached claim holds a current verdict; claims with no test never appear (that is health's `untested`). Also summarizes current verdicts.
Rules: test-verdicts

get_health.name: get_health
get_health.description:
The model's deterministic observability report. Headline: `tested` / `testable` / `untested` claim counts; then per node rollups, vagrant/stale flags, anchor coverage and state, link audit, `completeness`, `coverage` and `silentAnchors`. `node_id` scopes to one subtree with per-child summaries; omit for the whole-model summary. Use it to decide WHERE work is needed before reading subtrees.
Rules: health-reading, completeness-layered, loop-orient

node_id.description: Scope the report to one node's subtree; omit for the whole-model summary.
